# dsh-plugin-session-trash · Session Trash
English | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that adds **Move to trash** to each session's sidebar menu. Sessions
are not deleted outright: they go to a trash, where you can **restore** them from Settings → Sessio
n trash, or **delete them permanently after a second confirmation**. The trash is never emptied auto
r **delete them permanently after a second confirmation**. The trash is never emptied automatically.

## Install
**Desktop**: open **Plugins** in the sidebar → **Add plugin**, enter one of the following, choose **
Install**, then **Enable now** (a new plugin starts switched off):
- the GitHub address `https://github.com/ZZZZZZZ-ZZZZZ/dsh-session-trash`, or `github:ZZZZZZZ-ZZZZZ/

dsh-session-trash#v0.2.1` for a fixed version
- the npm package name `dsh-plugin-session-trash`
- th
e absolute path of a local package such as `/path/to/dsh-plugin-session-trash-0.2.1.tgz` (made by `p
path of a local package such as `/path/to/dsh-plugin-session-trash-0.2.1.tgz` (made by `pnpm pack`)
The repository includes the built `lib/`, so a GitHub install runs no build script. If DSH cannot re
ach GitHub, use a network that can; the npm mirror DSH offers serves npm packages, not GitHub reposi
Hub, use a network that can; the npm mirror DSH offers serves npm packages, not GitHub repositories.
Do not enter the source checkout: its `node_modules` holds development copies of DSH packages that w
ould shadow the ones DSH runs.
**Command line** (optional): install Desktop's own `dsh` command from the application menu **Manage
dsh Command…**, quit DSH completely, then run:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**Remove** it from the **Plugins** page, or quit DSH and run `dsh plugin --profile desktop remove ds
h-plugin-session-trash`. Sessions in the trash stay in `~/.dsh/session-trash/`; removing the plugin
does not delete them.
## Use
1. In a session's "…" menu choose **Move to trash** and confirm; the session leaves the sidebar. A s

ession opened in this run is hidden first and moves into the trash the next time DSH starts.
2. Open

**Settings → Session trash**:
- **Restore** puts the session back where it was, with its previous a

rchive and pin state;
- **Delete permanently** removes the local session logs after a second confirm

ation;
- **Empty trash** deletes every entry after confirmation, stopping at the first failure.
## Safety
| Rule | Detail |
| Sessions in use are never moved | Running work (a turn, subagents, background jobs, schedules) ref

uses the move; so does a session another DSH process writes (its `session.lock` is held) |
| Opened
sessions move at the next start | An idle session opened in this run is hidden at once (the official
archive) and moves into the trash at the next DSH start, before any session opens; every check stil
l applies then, and a move that cannot run waits for the following start. You can cancel it on the t

rash page meanwhile |
| Move, never copy | Moving to and from the trash is a same-volume `rename`; a

trash on another volume refuses |
| No recursive removal | Permanent deletion unlinks only the file
s DSH writes in a session directory (log generations, publish temporaries, `session.lock`) and remov

es directories with non-recursive `rmdir`; any other file refuses the whole deletion |
| Path checks
| Entry ids must be UUIDs; session directories and their parents must be plain directories (no symb

olic links) that resolve inside the session root; the trash must not be inside the session root |
|
Crash safety | A move is prepared in `.staging-<id>` and published by one rename; an interrupted mov

e is rolled back at the next start |
| Authenticated calls | The browser calls through DSH's `/api`

gateway (Typert Remote, connection-authenticated); no unauthenticated HTTP route is registered |
| O
fficial APIs | Hiding and restoring use the registry's `archiveSession` / `unarchiveSession` / `pinS
ession`; DSH's own storage is never rewritten |
Subagent sessions move and restore with their parent; forks are independent conversations and stay.
Project folders and workspace files are never touched.
## Configuration
| Field | Default | Meaning |
| `trashDirectory` | `<DSH home>/session-trash` | Trash directory; outside the session root and on t
y` | `<DSH home>/session-trash` | Trash directory; outside the session root and on the same volume |
## Permanent deletion is local only
**Delete permanently** removes the copies on this machine. It cannot reach what DSH has already sent
anently** removes the copies on this machine. It cannot reach what DSH has already sent to DeepSeek:
- With the official DeepSeek API, DSH uploads the session log along with each request by default (th
e official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-log-deepseek` plugin). Turning off **Settings → General → Uploa
d Session Log when using the official model API** stops later uploads only; turning it back on also

uploads what was recorded while it was off.
- Images sent to the official API are uploaded as files
that DSH asks DeepSeek to expire after 7 days; DSH does not guarantee their remote deletion.
This plugin makes no network requests and sends nothing anywhere.
## Known limitations
- A session opened in this run moves into the trash only at the next DSH start (a plugin cannot safe

ly release the write ownership DSH holds); until then it is hidden.
- Only session log directories a
re handled; attachments, caches, and spill files other features keep for a session stay where they a

re (see the Attachment Library below for attachment usage).
- Relies on the DSH 0.2.x JSONL director
y layout; re-verify after a DSH major upgrade.
